$comment: Phase-2 wave-1 OpenConnector ingestion config for the Nextcloud App Store catalog. Mirrors concurrentie-analyse/scripts/sync_nextcloud_marketplace.py (note: that script lives at scripts/sync_nextcloud_marketplace.py, one directory above scripts/sync/ - the file actually inside scripts/sync/ named sync_nextcloud_marketplace_installs.py is a different, downstream script that reads FROM an already-populated `nextcloud_marketplace` table to correlate apps against Specter's own `competitors` table; it does not talk to the App Store API at all and was not a usable model for this connector). Single unauthenticated GET, whole catalog in one response (no pagination) - apps.nextcloud.com/api/v1/apps.json returns a raw JSON array, not wrapped in an envelope. `usesPagination` is explicitly set to false: OpenConnector's engine only auto-disables pagination for `resultsPosition: '_object'` (single-object mode), not for `_root` (whole-array-at-root, which is this feed's actual shape) - leaving pagination on would have made the engine request a nonexistent page 2, which apps.json ignores and just returns the identical full catalog again, silently duplicating work up to DEFAULT_MAX_PAGES (50) times. Two deliberate simplifications vs. the Python script, both because MappingService's Twig+dot-notation engine has no loop/sort primitive: (1) `lastRelease`/`lastReleaseDate`/`license` assume the API returns `releases` newest-first and take index 0, whereas the Python script explicitly sorts releases by `created` date descending first; (2) `repository` uses a simplified 'website contains github.com' heuristic instead of the script's issueTracker-first-then-website logic. LIVE-VERIFIED END-TO-END 2026-07-05 on the isolated spectr-spike instance: the ORIGINAL blocking error (`The required property (source) is missing.`) was NOT a bug in this file - the mapping was already correct against this repo's current `marketplaceApp` schema (`sourceRef`/`appId`/`displayName` required); the spike's LIVE schema was a stale, unrelated v0.1.0 stub (`required: [name, source]`, only 7 shallow properties) never updated to this repo's v1.0.0 shape - fixed by re-importing `register/spectr_register.json` (see IMPORT.md's batch-3 section for the full diagnosis). Once fixed, ran `nextcloud-appstore-to-spectr-marketplaceapp` for real (single keyless request, whole catalog) against the real, live App Store catalog (690 apps, independently fetched and inspected beforehand) - `found: 690, created: 690` (confirmed via direct Postgres count once the request, which outlived the client's own timeout, finished server-side). Re-ran the same synchronization: `found: 690, updated: 690, created: 0` - same 690 target uuids reused, no duplicates. Sampled fields against 3 real apps (files_lock, shifts, group_default_quota) across every mapped property (name/category/author/downloads/rating/lastRelease/website/repository/license) - all matched the real catalog exactly, including a suspicious-looking but genuinely-real `ratingOverall: 0.5` on all three (confirmed present in the raw API response too, not a mapping artefact). The two flagged assumptions were checked live for the first time against the full real catalog: (1) `releases[0]` is newest-first for only 451/580 (78%) of apps with more than one release - 129/580 (22%) have a strictly newer release elsewhere in the array; Twig has no sort primitive so this cannot be fixed in the mapping, kept as a documented, quantified simplification. (2) Field presence across the full catalog: `translations.en.{name,summary,description}` and `categories` present on 690/690 (the `|default()` fallbacks are defensive, never actually triggered); `authors` missing/empty on 56/690 (the App Store's own gap, not this mapping's); `website` is always a string key (never null/missing), empty on 155/690 of which 0 have a non-empty `website` lacking `github.com` incorrectly counted - the `repository` heuristic degrades safely to `''` for all of them; `releases` empty on 51/690, safely defaulting `lastRelease`/`lastReleaseDate`/`license` to `''` via Twig's `|first|default()` chain on an empty array. No download-count field exists anywhere in the real API response, confirming the Python script's own hardcoded-0 comment.

objects.name: Nextcloud App Store
objects.description: The official Nextcloud App Store catalog API. Public, unauthenticated, single-shot (no pagination - the whole catalog comes back in one response). Feeds the spectr `marketplaceApp` register/schema via the nextcloud-appstore-to-spectr-marketplaceapp synchronization.

objects.name: Nextcloud App Store to Spectr Marketplace App
objects.description: Maps a raw App Store catalog entry onto the spectr `marketplaceApp` schema. Mirrors concurrentie-analyse/scripts/sync_nextcloud_marketplace.py's parse_app(). `downloads` is always mapped to a literal 0 because the App Store API does not expose install/download counts at all (the Python script hardcodes the same 0 with an explicit comment to that effect) - Specter's own download numbers come from a separate correlation step (sync_nextcloud_marketplace_installs.py) against its `competitors` table, which is out of scope for a direct App-Store-catalog ingestion connector.

mapping.name: {{ translations.en.name|default(id) }}
mapping.author: {{ authors|default([])|column('name')|join(', ') }}
mapping.repository: {{ (website is defined and 'github.com' in website) ? website : '' }}

objects.name: Nextcloud App Store to Spectr Marketplace App
objects.description: Wave-1 ingestion sync: Nextcloud App Store /apps.json (full catalog, single call) -> spectr register, marketplaceApp schema.

objects.name: Nextcloud App Store Weekly Sync
objects.description: Runs the nextcloud-appstore-to-spectr-marketplaceapp synchronization weekly, matching Specter's own tendril cadence.
